utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we have the appearances for the day. Starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everybody in and around the courtroom. Mark Harmon, Barney Thomas, and Carmela Javier for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours, and to everyone in the courtroom. Mr. Perisic is represented today in the courtroom by Milos Androvic, Mr. Gregor Guy-Smith, Novak Lukic, and our case manager, Daniela Tasic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much Mr. Lukic. Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you have a good rest last night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How do you feel today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not bad, thank you. Better than yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. As and when you feel like you need a break, don't hesitate to ask. Okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Once again I remind you that you are still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before we begin, Mr. Thomas and I agreed about two documents yesterday, that they can be given numbers. So perhaps we can tender them now and then begin. We had some problems that had to do with translation, and in the meantime we agreed on two documents. And I think Mr. Thomas is going to tell you which two documents this pertains to and perhaps then we can give these documents exhibit numbers and then continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, and I'm grateful for the assistance of my learned friend in this regard. The first document is P593 which was marked for identification. It was marked for identification on the basis, and perhaps it should come up in e-court, Your Honour, because there is something that should go into the record about this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's come up. You say it's P593. So it is an admitted document?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: It was given a number and marked for identification, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And if we could scroll to the bottom of both versions of the document, please. Now, sir, Your Honours may recall if we look at box 36, firstly in the B/C/S version there is a reference in Latin characters to BCP. And in the English translation, that was correctly translated as VSR, but then there is a reference "Army of the Serbian Republic," which is an addition made by the translator, and the Prosecution accepts, Your Honour, that that -- that VSR does not stand for Army of the Serbian Republic, and the document should be tendered on the basis that effectively Your Honour should not take any notice of that particular reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what must the Chamber make of the abbreviation VSR?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: On the face of the document, I don't believe there's been any testimony about what that abbreviation means, but what it does not mean is Army of the Serbian Republic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Army of Serbian Republic is VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you confirm, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Then that P593 marked for identification will be admitted into evidence as P593 subject to what Mr. Thomas has said.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The second document should also come up in e-court, that was also given an exhibit number marked for identification P610. Now, if we look at the English translation, Your Honours, in the section of the document that shows the addressees, Your Honours will see the reference to the command of the 35th POB Logistics Base. There was some confusion yesterday, the witness was not able to identify because of the quality of the reproduction on the screen whether the same reference existed in the B/C/S version. We have retrieved the original copy and shown it to my learned friends where they are in agreement that the reference does exist in the B/C/S version, and so we're agreed that the document can be tendered on the basis that the English translation is an accurate translation of the B/C/S version. We do have the original available if that is ever needed to be cited at any stage but because it has been retrieved from the vault for the purposes of this examination I think we are satisfied. Well, certainly the parties are happy to leave the scanned versions as they are so long as Your Honours are happy with that correction on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I did have the opportunity to look at the original document and to compare, and I agree that the document in this form is difficult to read in the B/C/S, but the English translation is quite adequate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. In that event, then P610 will be admitted into evidence and removed from being marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I'm afraid that I'm going to spend the bulk of today's cross-examination in private or closed session, and in any case as soon as I have begun I would like now to ask to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours, for the record we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, ma'am, thank you so much. I jumped the gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First, I drew attention to the date because there will be a series of these documents now with the same or similar date, that was my first intention, but in fact I'm interested in this information in box, I think it's box 13 where it says GS VJ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wanted to ask, witness, if he thought that that was the same handwriting, if the whole document is written in the same handwriting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems to be the same handwriting. Probably the handlers were filling in the list of receipt, so probably they filled it in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I cannot hear you through my headphones, I can only hear you like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to look at Exhibit 845.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we leave this, exhibit, Mr. Lukic, you're comparing handwritings and you are saying the handwritings are the same. I'd like to know which handwritings you are comparing, and I'd like to know from the witness on what basis he says that they are written by the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I went too fast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document, sir, that we have just looked at, the information on the sender should be filled in by the sender as a rule; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is what should be read in column, I don't see it very well, I think it's column 13 where it says GS VJ, that is that information, and also the military post, all of that should be filled in by the sender; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All these boxes of the sender are empty except for the one where it says GS VJ Kremna?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, if I may interrupt. I'm advised that at some stage the witness spoke while your microphone was on, Mr. Lukic, and the suspicion is that his voice might have gone out. I'm not quite sure how we resolve the problem of the voice that has already gone out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. The Registrar will resolve that. Thank you very much. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The senders column that you were explaining to us that should be filled in by the sender, this is -- only the terms "GS VJ" and "Kremna" are filled in, there is no date, there is no military post, there is no seal or stamp or the signature of the sender; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you would agree with me that the recipient who filled in the other boxes including the evidence number, the date of receipt, and the stamp of the receiver is the person who also filled in the information of the dispatcher or the sender of the items?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the Court would allow me to give a broader explanation, a couple of sentences more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Answer as you wish, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the handler, and there was such similar cases later about ammunition that came from Yugoslavia, if you would only get one copy and that copy would usually stay in a higher-ranking unit, specifically here we are talking about the Drina Corps, the handler would -- when he made a record of receipt, he would copy that from the list, then he would copy the right side, enter that into the log-book, and the person who received the goods would sign for it. However, in this list, if he did have the list, on the left side he also would need to fill in the precise details as to which military post these items came from. What most probably happened was that on the list there was an order of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, and perhaps for some reason he was lazy or he didn't put anything on the left side - I'm not going to go into the reasons - all he did was he wrote the GS VJ abbreviation, meaning that he did have some order from the General Staff, and then he would then additionally write the origin of the ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we make it so that the witness can see the entire document, and then he can tell us where exactly he sees this GS VJ abbreviation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's nothing specifically in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now can we show the witness a document; 585, exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, I've been trying to follow you, and I've not followed you clearly. But on the question comparing handwritings, I don't know when you talk about the left-hand side or the right-hand side how far you go to the left and how far you go to the right. But if you go to the B/C/S document that's before us, you'll see where the materiel is being listed, where we talk of 7.62 millimetre and then explain the materiel. Look at how that 7 is written, and go to the next column to the right, which has just got figures, and look at the 7s there. The 7s on that side have got a cross in the middle which the 7s on the left-hand side do not have. And if you look at the 7 on the right-hand top corner, the second from the end, 2117 is exactly the same -- well, not exactly the same, but it is similar to the 7s on the left. Similarly when you look at 7111. So I would like to know the basis on which it is being said that this form was filled in by one and the same person from beginning to end?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we will ask the question to clarify, Your Honour. Perhaps I was imprecise. What I would like to know in order to prove or to present my case is the facts that are entered under "Sender." Perhaps it's my mistake because I did not focus on the numbers. But what I am putting to the witness is that the information on the sender and the receiver was filled in in this particular case by the receiver?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which one is the sender and which one is the receiver? I can see sender, name and address of sender GS VJ. Which one is receiver?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The left-hand side of the form where it says GS VJ, that should be the sender. The receiver is box number 14 where it says "Command of the Drina Corps Tisca." So it is my case or my argument that this particular portion was filled by the same person. In other words, that the receiver filled in the date of receipt, as you can see top right there is the date 25/11/1993, so this -- and also the number under which these items were recorded, 2117-2-95 in Han Pijesak. All of this in the right upper corner, and also the military post of the receiver, 7111, and that this person actually filled also in the information for the sender, GS VJ. That is what I am put together the witness. I assume that the handlers or the administrators who were handling the ammunition, maybe two of them were working on it and one of them was filling out the quantities and so on. This in itself is not of great importance to me. What is important and what I'm trying to show here is that this was in fact filled out by the receiving party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe we will talk more about it at the time of argument. That's fine. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Witness, do you agree with me that this was -- that this name of the sender, GS VJ, was actually filled out by the receiving party, by the person who received the items?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We should focus on the top of the list, where it says "materiel list for" and then it says "receipt." If ammunition was sent to someone, then here in this heading it should say "materiel list for sending." In other words, the materiel list would have been filled in by the sending party. Here, whenever we see "receipt" it means that was filled in by the handler who received the items. And if we have both sides filled out, then that means that the list is the original list, the original copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I agree. My next question is very short. Was the receiving party authorised to fill in the boxes that are meant for the sending party? Just answer yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer with just yes and no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to hear your answer just in brief. And if you'd like to explain further, Mr. Thomas may want to put the questions to you in redirect. Now, I'm just asking you under the rules is the receiving party authorised to fill out any boxes meant for the sending party, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I am sorry, Your Honour, the witness has made it very clear that the answer cannot be given by a straightforward yes or no, and it's not an appropriate response to say if there's any qualification, we'll save it for re-examination. The witness has been very clear that he can't answer the question in that way. He should be permitted to answer it in the way which he considers it needs to be answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you may give us an answer but be careful we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... of that answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we are just discussing this in general, so I think it wouldn't really be necessary.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The administrator when he drew up this delivery sheet for receipt had to fill in the field where it says where the origin of the ammunition is from. So he did have the right or the authority to fill out -- to indicate where the ammunition had originated so that he would have this information about where the ammunition had come from, but this list is not clear. We've discussed this already yesterday, the GS VJ, it should have been noted at the bottom as a note, a comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another question. The handler or administrator, was he authorised to receive, to accept the materiel list that wasn't filled out by the issuing party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course he was allowed to because all he wanted to make sure was that the issue corresponded to what was written on the paper. So he just had to justify whatever he had in stock, that had to correspond to what was on the paper. The handler really nobody authorised him for anything else nor asked him to do anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but if the materiel list is blank, then he wouldn't know where the materiel had come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if the materiel list was blank, he couldn't know where the materiel or ammunition had come from unless he was told by one of his superiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Now, let's take a look at P594 MFI. Excuse me, just a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I resume? Could we see now briefly the following document, 577.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I got no translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we now briefly see document P577 on the screens. So let's -- just briefly, can you see an order from the Chief of General Staff anywhere on this form?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you cannot see the number of such an order anywhere on this form.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we just scroll this a bit to the right so the date appears.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will just read this out for you and you will tell us. This was received by the command of the Drina Corps on the 23rd of November, 1993; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see document P578, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this is an identical document that the command of the Drina Corps received on the same day, at least that's what it says here, from the VJ, from Bogovadja, something, and that the same person filled out this form, the portion at least where the issuing party is mentioned; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, but it doesn't say the Chief of General Staff, it just says the Yugoslav Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see document P574.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A day before on the 21st of -- on the 22nd of November, 1994 [as interpreted], the same command, the Drina Corps, confirms that it had received this ammunition, and as the issuing party mention is made of GS VJ, the General Staff, Lunjevica, and the same person filled out both the sender and the receiver part of the document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Most of these lists were filled out by the same handler or administrator, the ones we've seen so far.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you can confirm that there is no mention made here of any order by the Chief of General Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is no confirmation anywhere that this was issued by the orders of the Chief of General Staff. All it says is GS VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another document, P572. Exhibit 572.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The same question for you, sir. The date here -- if we can just scroll it to the right a bit so we can see the date. The Drina Corps command, the 22nd of November, 1993; in other words, the same date as the previous document. There is also no order from the Chief of Staff of the General Staff anywhere in this document; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No order is mentioned, but the list that we can see now, as we can see the dates are all similar or maybe even the same, which means that if we have the same lists dated on the same day and coming from different military posts, this means that on the same day ammunition was received from various warehouses, various military posts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in none of these documents did we see the military post of the issuing party; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again we see that the same person filled out both sides, the issuing party side and the receiving party side. Can we just scroll it now a bit to the left to compare.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is standard. The same person filled out this list and completed this form.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have a correction in the transcript. Page 42, line 11. 1994 is mentioned as the year, but in fact from the documents we could see that it was 1993, and I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I won't go through the documents. There are three remaining exhibits here, I won't go through them all with the witness, but I do have a question for you, Witness, regarding these documents. Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please move into private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We saw in these documents a little earlier that practically they all were compiled on the same date or thereabouts. They were all from the 22nd from the 25th of November in 1993, and they were all received by the Drina Corps; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is how it's stated in the documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, or the day before yesterday as well, you confirmed that supplies and deliveries from Yugoslavia were more frequent when there were more offensive activities or intensified conflict in a certain territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall that at the end of 1993 there was intensive fighting in the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was around the area of Skelani in Srebrenica, but I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let's see P594, page 2, please. Could it be retrieved on the screen. And the previous -- preceding page in the B/C/S version, please, I'm sorry. Your Honours, this is the linguistic problem that you used to have, so I'd like to clarify it with the witness, and I've discussed this with the interpreters, and I hope that we are going to find a common word for the word "discharge," "razduzenje."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, it says here --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this document from yesterday, and I remember what it states.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. At the beginning of today's session I omitted to mention that Judge David is still indisposed and that we are sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis. May the record show that we are still sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis today for the same reasons. Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'll defer to Mr. Harmon in terms of the arrangements for next week, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll need to go into private session to discuss the arrangements for next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned sine die at
